ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a net of a triangular prism, with the main body being three side-by-side rectangles. Their upper sides are labeled from left to right as YX, XW, WU; on the lower sides from left to right there are points such as P, Q, S, T. Above the upper side WU of the right rectangle is connected triangle WUV, and below the lower side QS of the central rectangle is connected triangle QRS. Reasoning: A triangular prism has three rectangular side faces enclosing a triangular end face. When folded, the corresponding edges of the three rectangles will respectively become the three sides of the triangular end face WUV. Edge WU is already connected to one side WU of the triangle; the adjacent upper side XW will fold to correspond to WV; the remaining upper side YX will fold to correspond to UV. Therefore, the line that forms an edge together with UV after folding is XY.

method.method_draft: Read the image as a net with three rectangles in a horizontal strip. Their top edges, from left to right, are YX, XW, and WU. A triangle with vertices W, V, U is attached along WU. From the text, use that the solid is a three-sided prism, so the three rectangular faces wrap around a triangular end. In the folded prism, the top edges of the three rectangles must become the three sides of the triangular face WUV. Since WU is already one side of that triangle, the adjacent top edge XW folds to side WV, and the remaining top edge YX folds to side UV. Therefore the line forming an edge together with UV is XY.

First use the lower triangle to establish which rectangle corresponds to which triangular side: the middle rectangle is attached to side QS, the left rectangle must meet side QR, and the right rectangle must meet side RS when the prism is folded. The top edge of the left rectangle is XY, so UV folds together with XY.
